topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: These remarks introduce the lecture topic and outline the key learning outcomes regarding cellular transformation and cancer genetics.

topics.label: Discovery of Oncogenes via Tumor Viruses and Transformation Assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the history of tumor virology, the mechanism of retroviral oncogene capture, and laboratory assays developed to measure cell transformation.

topics.label: Classification and Mechanisms of Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressor Genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the classification of cancer-driving mutations and explore the mechanistic effects of alterations in tumor suppressors and oncogenes such as Rb and p53.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Consequences of Genetic Instability in Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the causes and cellular consequences of sequence instability and chromosomal instability arising from defective DNA repair, replication errors, and mitotic abnormalities.

topics.label: Multistep Tumor Progression and Hereditary Cancer Predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how sequential accumulation of mutations drives cancer progression and how inherited germline mutations accelerate this multi-step pathway.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Recommended Reading
topics.groupedBecause: These closing remarks conclude the lecture, summarize coverage of the learning outcomes, and provide recommended reading.
